annotations.summary: The song title: 'It Snowed in Beijing Last Night' by Lambert. Sets a melancholic, cinematic scene of snowfall in Beijing as the central image.
annotations.cultural_context: Snowfall in Beijing is a recurring romantic/lonely motif in Chinese pop and indie music, often symbolizing separation, memory, or the quiet ending of a relationship.

annotations.summary: Production credit line naming the executive producers (Zheng Hanwen and Shen Bing of the Flowsixteen label/production team).
allusions: Flowsixteen — a Chinese music production/label team credited across multiple Mandarin pop releases
annotations.cultural_context: Standard bilingual (Chinese/English) credit formatting typical of Chinese streaming platform lyric sheets.

annotations.summary: Copyright notice stating that covers or unauthorized use of the song are prohibited without permission.
annotations.cultural_context: Common rights-protection disclaimer embedded in Chinese music platform lyrics, reflecting China's tighter enforcement of music copyright on platforms like NetEase Cloud Music and QQ Music since ~2015.

annotations.summary: The narrator observes that it snowed in Beijing last night — the song's central image and title, establishing time, place, and emotional setting.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Snow functions as the song's controlling metaphor: coldness, distance, and emotional desolation. Beijing's winter snow mirrors the narrator's inner chill after losing someone, a classic Chinese pop convention where weather externalizes mood (借景抒情).
annotations.cultural_context: Beijing in winter is a heavily loaded setting in Chinese urban pop — associated with migrant dreams, departure, and transience (北漂 culture). Snow arriving silently overnight parallels the silent departure of a lover.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Comparable to Swift's weather-as-emotional-state device (e.g., 'it's a cruel summer,' rain imagery in 'Clean' or the snow in 'tis the damn season'), where meteorology frames the entire emotional narrative.

annotations.summary: The narrator wonders whether the person they miss is also looking out through a window — presumably at the same snow — imagining a shared moment across distance.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The window is a liminal frame: a boundary between the interior (self, memory) and the exterior (the world, the lost person). Both parties gazing 'through the window' at the same snow creates an imagined visual connection despite physical separation.
annotations.cultural_context: High-rise window-gazing is a distinctly urban Chinese image — dense apartment living in cities like Beijing makes the window the primary interface with weather and the city, reinforcing the theme of isolation amid millions.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Echoes Swift's device of imagining an ex's parallel experience ('Do you miss the rogue / who coaxed you into paradise?' in 'The Black Dog'; the shared-sky imagery in 'Hoax').

annotations.lyric_text: 看那漫天的冰霜在慢慢降落
annotations.summary: Describing the vast, sky-filling frost and snow slowly falling — the slow descent emphasizing the heaviness and inevitability of the emotional atmosphere.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The slow-falling snow mirrors the slow, inescapable descent of the narrator into sadness. '漫天' (filling the whole sky) conveys the overwhelming scale of the feeling — the loss saturates everything, the way snow covers an entire city.

annotations.summary: The title line returns as a refrain, re-anchoring the song after the imagined shared glance — the fact of the snow now carrying the weight of the narrator's unspoken feelings.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: As a repeated hook, the snow line transforms from observation into incantation: repeating it mimics rumination — the mind circling the same cold fact, the same cold loss.
annotations.cultural_context: Repetition of a plain declarative sentence (北京昨夜下了雪) is characteristic of Chinese ballad songwriting (e.g., 陈奕迅, 薛之谦 traditions), where understatement carries maximal feeling.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Comparable to Swift's use of a repeated geographic-weather hook like 'Welcome to New York' or the recurring 'August sipped away' — a place/time marker that deepens with each return.

annotations.lyric_text: 我又不自主地难过渴望
annotations.summary: Confronted again by the snow, the narrator admits they involuntarily fall back into sadness and longing — they cannot control the resurgence of emotion.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The involuntariness ('不自主') personifies grief as something that seizes the narrator — like weather, it arrives without consent. The snow acts as a trigger, a conditioned stimulus for heartbreak.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Resonant with Swift's recurring theme of uncontrollable emotional relapse — 'I knew you'd linger like a tattoo kiss' ('Dress'), or 'I can go anywhere I want, anywhere I want, just not home' ('This Is Me Trying').

annotations.lyric_text: 感觉寒冷时 能够想起 我
annotations.summary: The narrator's deepest wish: that when the other person feels cold, they will remember the narrator — the one who once kept them warm.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The emotional logic is inverted from the snow metaphor: cold = absence of the narrator's love; warmth = the narrator's presence. To be remembered when cold is to remain functionally alive in the ex's life as an internal source of heat.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Mirrors Swift's plea to remain in an ex's memory ('please don't ever become a stranger whose laugh I could recognize anywhere' in 'New Year's Day'; 'I hope you think of me' in 'I Wish You Would').

annotations.summary: The narrator reflects on the warmth they gave the person in the past — love, care, and comfort now reduced to memory.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: '温暖' (warmth) is the direct counter-image to the song's snow: the narrator casts their past love as the heat that once melted winter. Its past-tense framing ('过去曾') underscores that the warmth is a spent resource.

annotations.summary: The closing admission: without you now, there is nothing to be done — a resigned acceptance of the pain as the song ends where it began, in the snow.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The plain statement '没你很无奈' (without you, helpless/resigned) strips away all metaphor for the final line — matching the emotional exhaustion of someone who has run out of words, letting the cold fact stand alone.
annotations.cultural_context: The understated, almost conversational closing line reflects the Chinese ballad preference for '留白' (leaving blank space) — the listener completes the grief.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Similar to Swift's understated resignation endings — 'I just wanted you to know' ('All Too Well'), where simplicity after complexity lands the emotional blow.

annotations.summary: 分手后留下的是加倍的孤独——一个人时反而比恋爱时更空虚。
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 「双倍率的孤单」(double-rate loneliness) 把孤独量化成游戏术语般的倍数概念：恋爱时两人共享的寂寞是 1，失去对方后回忆叠加现实，孤独翻倍。将抽象情感数值化是 Lambert 所在的中文 R&B/说唱圈常见的写法。
annotations.wordplay: 「双倍率」挪用电子游戏/抽卡语境中的『double rate(双倍掉落率)』一词，把游戏黑话嵌入情歌，形成口语化的俏皮感——掉的不再是装备，而是 loneliness。
annotations.cultural_context: 中国 Z 世代网络语言与游戏术语渗透进流行音乐歌词的典型现象。

annotations.lyric_text: Don't lie girl oh 我知道
annotations.summary: 别骗我了女孩，我都知道——你嘴上放下了，其实心里还没有。
annotations.wordplay: 中英混排(code-switching):英文祈使句『Don't lie』直插中文歌词，形成语气上的突兀感，模拟口语中急切抢话的状态。
annotations.cultural_context: 中英夹杂是中生代及新生代华语 R&B、嘻哈的标志性语言风格(可对比 Higher Brothers、KnowKnow 等的语码转换 code-switching 传统)。

annotations.summary: 你也很烦恼吧——为什么我总是忘不掉。
我为什么总是在你心里打转，挥之不去。
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 「转」(spinning/turning) 把记忆具象成一个绕着心旋转的物体——像陀螺、像唱片、像循环播放的画面。旋转意象同时暗示 obsessive rumination(反刍式思念),想停却停不下来的眩晕感。
annotations.wordplay: 「转」双关:既是『旋转、打转』,也暗指音乐『转』播、转了一圈又回来,呼应歌中萦绕的旋律感。
annotations.emotional_tone: 执念 眩晕般的思念

annotations.summary: 忘记一个人,远没有嘴上说的那么容易。
allusions: 「没那么简单」高度呼应黄小琥 2009 年金曲《没那么简单》(Not That Simple)的歌名与核心句式——该曲唱的正是『相爱没有那么容易,每个人有他的脾气』,此处借经典情歌句式表达遗忘之难。
annotations.cultural_context: 《没那么简单》是华语 KTV 时代关于『放下很难』的国民级情感模板,化用其句式能瞬间唤起听众的集体记忆。

annotations.lyric_text: 约好下个冬天还能牵你手
annotations.summary: 我们约定好,下一个冬天还能像从前一样牵着手。
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 「下个冬天」(next winter) 象征关系修复的时间窗口——以季节为单位许下承诺,把复合的希望寄托在未来的一个完整循环之后。冬天既是两人故事发生的背景(北京下雪的冬夜),也被重塑为重逢之约的见证。

annotations.summary: 就算在大雪里也继续往前走,不停下。
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 「大雪中接着走」(walking on through the heavy snow) 是共渡难关的经典隐喻:风雪代表感情中的外部压力与困境,『接着走』表示不离不弃、并肩前行。画面与歌名『北京昨夜下了雪』的雪景意象闭环。

annotations.summary: 我保证不会再对你冷淡、疏远。
annotations.wordplay: 「冷漠」(cold/indifferent) 与全曲的冰雪意象形成刻意的语义反差:雪是冷的,但人不能再冷——用『冷』字同时点出天气与态度,是贯穿全曲的 cold 双关链条的一环。

annotations.lyric_text: 但愿 冰雪 能够
annotations.summary: 只愿这片冰雪,能够……(承接下句:治愈你的伤口)。
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 「冰雪」(ice and snow) 在此完成意象反转:通常象征寒冷、伤害、关系冰冻的冰雪,被祈愿成为疗伤之物——以冷治伤,如同冰敷(an ice compress)止痛。三连的停顿(但愿/冰雪/能够)模拟祈祷般的迟疑与虔诚。

annotations.lyric_text: 愈合你伤口 不用再多的理由
annotations.summary: 让冰雪愈合你的伤口吧,不需要再找任何借口或解释。
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 「伤口」(wound) 是情感创伤的具象化——不是肉体的伤,而是被冷落、被伤害后的心伤。冰雪『愈合』伤口延续了上一行的意象反转:曾经造成冰冻伤害的东西,如今成为疗愈的媒介,暗示伤害者(叙述者)想亲手弥补自己造成的裂痕。
annotations.wordplay: 「不用再多的理由」双关:既指不必再有解释就能原谅,也指爱不需要理由——把 apology(道歉)与 unconditional love(无条件的爱)压缩进一句。
annotations.emotional_tone: 忏悔 释然 温柔

annotations.summary: The speaker resolves to keep pursuing a dream that was left unfinished — likely the relationship or a shared future that ended prematurely.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: '没做完的梦' (the unfinished dream) is a metaphor for an interrupted relationship or abandoned shared plans — dreams as aspirations for the future that were cut short.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Comparable to Swift's recurring device of the 'unfinished' — e.g., 'the story of us' breaking down mid-sentence, or 'Come Back... Be Here' where a relationship ends before it can complete its arc.

annotations.summary: The title line: it snowed in Beijing last night. The snowfall triggers the entire chain of memory and longing that follows.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Snow functions as the emotional catalyst — a sudden, silent change in the landscape mirroring how memories arrive uninvited. '昨夜' (last night) pins the longing to a specific, recent moment.
allusions: Beijing as a symbolic urban landscape in Chinese Mandopop — the city of ambition, migration, and lost love (echoing songs like 汪峰's Beijing imagery)
annotations.cultural_context: Beijing's winter snow is a culturally loaded image for young Chinese people — many migrate to Beijing for work or school, so snow there often signifies displacement and missing someone far away.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Functions like 'the autumn leaves falling down like pieces into place' in All Too Well — weather as the trigger for involuntary memory.

annotations.lyric_text: 你是否也透过窗口看那漫天的
annotations.summary: The speaker wonders aloud whether the absent person is also watching the same snowfall through their window right now.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The window (窗口) is a liminal metaphor — both people are separated by glass/walls/distance, yet briefly connected by looking at the same sky.
annotations.wordplay: The line ends mid-image ('漫天的' — 'the sky-filling...') with a deliberate enjambment; the thought hangs suspended like the snow itself.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Mirrors 'you call me up again just to break me like a promise' from All Too Well — the ache of imagining what the other person is doing; also evokes the 'are you somewhere feeling lonely too' structure of many Swift ballads.

annotations.lyric_text: 冰霜 在慢慢 降落
annotations.summary: The suspended image resolves: frost and snow slowly descending from the sky.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: '慢慢降落' (slowly falling) mirrors the slow settling of grief — emotions descending and accumulating on the speaker like snow on a city. The coldness of 冰霜 (frost/ice) externalizes internal emotional coldness.
annotations.wordplay: The drawn-out delivery ('慢慢 降落') phonetically enacts the slow falling it describes.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Comparable to the snowfall imagery in 'tis the damn season — snow as the atmosphere of a reunion/loss that can only exist in memory.

annotations.summary: The title refrain returns, now heavier with accumulated feeling — the snowfall statement has transformed into a confession.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: As a refrain, the snow is no longer just weather — repetition converts it into the emotional event itself: the snow IS the memory of the person.
annotations.wordplay: Exact repetition of line 31 functions as a chorus-anchor; in Chinese ballad structure (主歌/副歌), this is the hook that the ear waits for.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Swift uses identical-refrain-as-emotional-shift similarly in tracks like 'Clean' ('when I was drowning...') where each return of the line deepens rather than repeats meaning.

annotations.lyric_text: 我又不自主地难过渴望
annotations.summary: The speaker admits they cannot help themselves — sadness and longing arrive involuntarily.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: '不自主' (not self-controlled/involuntary) frames emotion as a force that possesses the speaker — grief as something done TO them, echoing the snow falling outside their control.
annotations.wordplay: The compressed pairing '难过渴望' (grieve-long) jams two emotions into one breath, suggesting they're indistinguishable at this point.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Resonates with Swift's 'I think I've seen this film before' — the involuntary, scripted quality of returning pain in exile it / the 1.

annotations.lyric_text: 感觉寒冷时能够想起 我
annotations.summary: A fragile wish: 'when you feel cold, may you think of me.' The speaker hopes to persist in the other person's memory as a source of warmth.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Warmth/cold (温暖/寒冷) as the central emotional metaphor of the song — the speaker's love is reframed as body heat given away, now that the recipient is gone, all that remains is the cold.
annotations.wordplay: The isolated final '我' (me) — separated by a pause — lands as a small, exposed single syllable, enacting the speaker's loneliness grammatically.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Directly parallels 'you keep his shirt, he keeps his word' logic — wanting to be the retained object of memory; also 'long for all the warmth you gave me' energy from Back to December.

annotations.summary: The speaker recalls the warmth they once gave — confirming line 36's wish is rooted in a real, past devotion.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: '温暖' (warmth) is the song's core concrete-abstract metaphor: actual emotional care described as physical heat, set against the literal cold of the Beijing snow.
annotations.wordplay: The past-tense marker '曾' (once) does heavy lifting — a single syllable converting warmth into something irrevocably finished.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Comparable to 'you made a rebel of a careless man's careful daughter' — cataloging what one gave in a relationship as proof the love was real.

annotations.lyric_text: 现在 没你 很无奈
annotations.summary: Now, without you, there's nothing to be done — a flat, resigned statement of helplessness.
annotations.wordplay: The stark '没你' (without you) — a negated pronoun with no verb — grammatically enacts absence: the sentence itself is missing something.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: The plain-spoken resignation recalls 'so it goes' or the deadpan delivery of 'it's fine, I'm fine' structures Swift uses when pain exceeds eloquence.

annotations.summary: The closing line: what remains is loneliness at double the rate — solitude squared, as if the missing person's absence also stole the comfort of having once been together.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 孤单 (loneliness) is quantified with '双倍率' (double rate) — an almost mathematical, spreadsheet-like metaphor for grief, as if loneliness accrues interest over time.
annotations.wordplay: '双倍率' is an unusual, quasi-technical coinage (rate of doubling / at 200%) — borrowing the language of finance/data for emotion, making the pain feel precise and modern; the coldness of the term contrasts with the warmth (温暖) mourned earlier in the song.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Comparable to 'two paper airplanes flying' inverted — Swift often quantifies love (one for the money, two for the show) and loss; here the doubling metaphor echoes 'the burgundy on my t-shirt when you splashed your wine into it' where small measures carry total feeling.

annotations.lyric_text: Don't lie girl oh 我知道
annotations.summary: The singer tells the girl not to deny it — he already knows what she truly feels. A direct, intimate appeal across a language barrier of English and Mandarin.
annotations.wordplay: Code-switching between English ('Don't lie girl oh') and Mandarin ('我知道' — 'I know') is a signature device in Chinese hip-hop/R&B (cf. higher brothers, KnowKnow). The switch softens the confrontation: the English is playful and pleading, the Chinese lands the certainty.
annotations.cultural_context: Mandarin-English code-switching is a hallmark of China's post-2015 hip-hop wave (after shows like The Rap of China 中国有嘻哈), which Lambert凌杰 emerged from.

annotations.summary: Half of a two-line thought: 'You're also annoyed (by it) — why is it that I...' The enjambment creates a breathless, unresolved feeling.
annotations.wordplay: 烦 (fán) means both 'annoyed/bothered' and, colloquially, 'troubled/intruded upon' — he knows his memory intrudes on her peace of mind, and there's a hint of satisfaction in that.

annotations.lyric_text: 总在你心里转 忘记没那么简单
annotations.summary: '...always spinning around in your heart — forgetting me isn't that simple.' He believes he still occupies her thoughts, and that moving on is harder than she pretends.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: '总在你心里转' (constantly turning/spinning in your heart) — the image of a record on a turntable or a thought on loop: he is stuck on repeat in her mind, an earworm she can't skip.
allusions: '没那么简单' echoes the hook of 黄小琥's 2010 hit 《没那么简单》 ('Not That Simple'), a karaoke staple about love being anything but easy — a wink Chinese listeners would catch instantly.
annotations.wordplay: 转 (zhuàn, to spin/revolve) ties the turntable image to the recurring musical refrain — the song itself keeps 'turning' back to the same plea.

annotations.summary: The song's central refrain and invitation: stop overthinking the past and just be present with him in the falling snow.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Dancing in the snow is an image of carefree, ephemeral romance — snow melts quickly, so the moment must be seized. Snow also symbolizes purity and a blank slate: this dance is a chance to start clean before winter (and Christmas) ends.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: A Swift parallel: 'dancing' as the apex of romantic abandon runs through her work ('Long Live,' 'Dancing With Our Hands Tied'), and snow functions similarly in 'Christmas Tree Farm' and 'Back To December' — winter as the emotional season of a relationship's make-or-break.

annotations.lyric_text: 下次见你别再 沉默着
annotations.summary: 'Next time we meet, don't stay silent anymore.' He's asking her to break the cold-war quiet between them.
annotations.wordplay: The caesura splitting 别再 / 沉默着 ('don't... stay silent') mimics the hesitation and gap in communication he's describing — the lyric itself goes quiet mid-phrase.

annotations.summary: Repetition of the plea with the affectionate 'girl' address — an intensifier, not new information.
annotations.wordplay: Repetition here functions the way a hook does in R&B: the doubling of 别再沉默着 turns a request into a near-desperate mantra, with the English 'girl' softening it into intimacy.

annotations.summary: Refrain returns — the repeated invitation to let go and share the moment, now carrying the weight of his plea against her silence.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Same snow-dance metaphor as line 43, but on repetition it shifts from spontaneity to argument: the dance becomes his answer to the communication breakdown.

annotations.summary: 'In a few weeks it'll be Christmas' — he's marking the calendar, using the holiday as leverage and a deadline for reconciliation.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Christmas functions as a metonymy for couple-dom in contemporary Chinese urban pop: a holiday that demands a companion. The countdown ('再过几周', just a few more weeks) turns the season into an ultimatum of tenderness.
annotations.cultural_context: Christmas in mainland China is largely a secular, commercial and romantic holiday — couples' dinners, gift exchanges, and 'Christmas Eve = date night' are standard in first-tier cities like Beijing, the song's setting. Invoking it frames the relationship as something to secure before the socially couple-coded holiday arrives.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: Compare Taylor's deployment of Christmas as relationship shorthand in 'Christmas Tree Farm' and the holiday stakes of 'Back To December.'

annotations.summary: 'I don't want to be alone anymore' — the emotional thesis of the song laid bare: beneath the swagger, this is a loneliness confession.
annotations.wordplay: 一个人 (one person / alone) — the simplest phrase in the song, deliberately plain after layers of English and metaphor. The plainness IS the device: the bravado drops.
annotations.cultural_context: 都市孤独 (urban loneliness) is a dominant theme in Chinese Gen-Z music and media — the '一人食' (eating alone) phenomenon and solo-living aesthetics made loneliness a culturally legible, even fashionable, subject for young artists in Beijing and Shanghai.

annotations.lyric_text: 约好下个冬天还能牵你手
annotations.summary: 'Let's agree that next winter I can still hold your hand' — the closing line converts the plea into a promise, projecting the relationship a full year forward.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Holding hands in winter is metonymy for continuity and warmth against the cold — the hand as the one warm point in a frozen Beijing. '下个冬天' (next winter) stretches a single snow dance into a yearly ritual, framing love as seasonal renewal.
annotations.wordplay: 还能 (still be able to) is the quiet pivot of the whole song — it doesn't say 'I will,' it says 'may I still,' smuggling uncertainty and the fear of losing her into an otherwise confident closing line.
annotations.cultural_context: The lyric cycles back to the title image (北京昨夜下了雪 — 'It Snowed in Beijing Last Night'), completing the song's structure: one Beijing snowfall becomes a vow measured in winters, a distinctly northern-Chinese romantic temporality.
annotations.taylor_swift_context: The 'still be able to' construction recalls Taylor's conditional future-tense romantic vows ('Call It What You Want,' the 'would've, could've, should've' anxiety of 'Right Where You Left Me') — both artists use grammatical tentateness to encode relational fear inside a love song.

annotations.summary: In the heavy snow, he keeps moving forward; hardship becomes weather to walk through rather than a reason to stop.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The blizzard works as an external image of emotional pressure or a difficult chapter in love; continuing to walk suggests perseverance despite numbness, distance, or pain.
annotations.cultural_context: Winter snow in northern Chinese cities is often romanticized in Mandopop as a backdrop for memory, separation, and quiet devotion.

annotations.summary: He promises not to become cold or indifferent toward the person he loves.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 冷漠 resonates with the snow imagery: emotional coldness and literal coldness are placed side by side, making the promise feel like warmth held against winter.
annotations.wordplay: 冷漠 literally means cold/indifferent; in a snow song it gains a double edge of emotional detachment versus freezing weather.

annotations.lyric_text: 但愿冰雪能够愈合你伤口
annotations.summary: He wishes the ice and snow could somehow close or soothe the beloved’s wounds.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: There is a deliberate paradox: ice usually hardens, numbs, or cuts, but here it is imagined as a healing salve—like wanting pain to crystallize cleanly so it can finally stop hurting.

annotations.summary: No further justification is needed; the choice to stay or continue is enough.
He wants to resume the dream they had not finished—an interrupted future, plan, or love.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The unfinished dream stands for suspended possibility: a relationship paused by circumstances, a shared life imagined but not yet lived.

annotations.summary: The title-hook returns: snow fell over Beijing last night, marking the scene with memory and longing.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Beijing under snow becomes a remembered emotional landscape—beautiful, silent, and distancing—where private feeling is projected onto a citywide event.
annotations.cultural_context: Beijing snow often functions in Chinese pop as cinematic atmosphere: modern urban loneliness softened by white, hushed imagery.

annotations.lyric_text: 你是否也透过窗口看那漫天的
annotations.summary: He wonders whether the other person is also watching, through a window, the vast sky filling with snow.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The window is a threshold between intimacy and separation: both people may be seeing the same snow, but from different rooms, cities, or emotional positions.
annotations.wordplay: The line ends mid-image on 漫天的, creating an enjambment that lets the snowfall spill into the next line.

annotations.lyric_text: 冰霜 在慢慢 降落
annotations.summary: Frost and snow descend slowly, as if time itself has softened.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: The slow fall turns weather into suspended feeling: coldness is not violent but gradual, matching the way grief or desire settles in.

annotations.summary: The refrain repeats, making the snowfall feel less like an event than a loop of memory.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: Repetition mirrors rumination: the same image returns because the feeling has not been resolved; Beijing becomes a witness that keeps silent while emotion accumulates.

annotations.lyric_text: 我又不自主地难过渴望
annotations.summary: Again, involuntarily, he feels both sorrow and desire at once.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 难过 and 渴望 are fused into one reflex: missing someone is not pure sadness but a pull toward them, showing love persisting beneath pain.
annotations.wordplay: 不自主 emphasizes loss of control—the snow triggers feeling before reason can intervene.

annotations.lyric_text: 感觉寒冷时 能够想起 我
annotations.summary: The speaker expresses a humble, tender wish: that when the listener feels cold (literally, in the Beijing winter snow, or metaphorically, in emotional loneliness), they will remember the speaker. It is a plea to remain present in someone's memory even after separation.
annotations.metaphor_analysis: 寒冷 (cold) operates on two levels: literal cold from the Beijing snow referenced in the title, and emotional coldness/loneliness. Being 'remembered when cold' positions the speaker as a source of warmth — a mental refuge the listener can return to. The conditional structure (能够想起 — 'may you be able to recall') suggests uncertainty about whether that memory will endure, softening the line into vulnerability rather than a demand.
annotations.wordplay: The sentence is deliberately fragmented (感觉寒冷时 / 能够想起 / 我) with pauses isolating 我 (me/I) at the end — the pronoun stands alone as the emotional payload of the entire line, emphasizing that the speaker's only wish is simply to be remembered.
